convoLines.text: "We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the east treeline."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the east treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Mario owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Anyway — I should get going."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone? Allegedly."
"I get it. Solitude's a resource too. Scarcer than food, some days."
"I go to the treeline edge and count my breaths. Ten of them. That's my alone. Then I come back — alone is a luxury, and also a little bit a lie. But what do I know."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Well — Still on needing to be alone."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
The silence stretches a beat too long. They study their hands.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Can I tell you something? I've been skimming extra food. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
I don't need a statue. I need one good story that outlives me.
"Everyone gets forgotten eventually. I'm negotiating for later rather than sooner."
"Do something worth retelling. That's the whole plan. The rest is logistics."
"Still on what they want."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Right. Sorry, I go on about it. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Since Mario died... I keep expecting to see Mario at the fire. Stupid."
You show them Mayapple — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Alright. Catch you later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You take those walks that don't need to happen. Still breathing your own air?"
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"That again?" Finn sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"People are smiling. I forgot what that looked like."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on cheer."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Good times. What did you want to talk about?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The Oath. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I do the small things right. The big things notice."
You show them Wild Black Cherry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Meet me at the south slope below the meadow and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "They took you — The Echo, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"Same as always: we endure."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I asked Mario about the pantry run — Mario's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the old burn east of camp in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"The Echo. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I wake before anyone else. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
You show them Wild Onion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
